about: What a seat must see for each prompt, worked by hand from the rule each case's why names.
The lessons are posted in this order, each a standing lesson with its id and stamp.
The lookalikes tie on every word the pack and the hook score, and are posted in reverse id order, so only packset's order for a tie, by id, puts look-00 first.
A case's shows lists the lessons the hook prints, in the order it prints them.
A stand-in for packset-embed: a text's vector counts its words in each group.
A prompt with none of these words has a zero vector, so the pack sends no dense ballot and the hook ranks by words alone.

cases.name: covers-the-prompt
why: No word of the prompt is in an encoder group, so the hook ranks by words.
ci-secret, pnpm and every lookalike say registry, rejected and token, and BM25 puts ci-secret, the shortest, first.
The lookalikes tie on words and length, so packset's order for a tie, by id, puts look-00 and look-01 next, and the hook hands over three.
Printed oldest first: ci-secret from January, then the two lookalikes, which share a stamp and keep their order.

cases.name: alias-in-a-full-window
cases.prompt: yarn: the registry rejected my token
why: yarn and pnpm are one alias group in the hook's subject test, so pnpm covers the most of the prompt.
pnpm is the longest lesson, so only the pack's lexical ballot keeps it, last of the twenty the hook asks for, as the tied lesson whose id sorts first.
ci-secret comes next by BM25 and look-00 by id.
Printed oldest first: ci-secret from January, pnpm from February, look-00 from October.

cases.name: failure-note

failure.error: E401: the registry rejected the token

why: The note searches on the command and its error, so it reads the window alias-in-a-full-window reads.
It prints the most relevant first and does not sort by age: pnpm by its alias, ci-secret by BM25, look-00 by id.

cases.name: always-names-no-subject
why: always is a rule word, not a subject.
squash says always and the pack's two ballots both name it, but it shares no other word with the prompt; fmt says cargo and fmt.

cases.name: paraphrase
cases.prompt: how often do we change our cryptographic credentials
why: No lesson says a word of the prompt, so only the dense ballot names any.
The prompt counts one word in each group and so does signing: cosine 1 at dense rank 1, past DENSE_ALONE_AT, 0.66, which a hit that shares no word must reach.
ceremony counts key and signing, cosine 2/sqrt(6) = 0.82, at dense rank 2.
Its key names the subject through the hook's alias group of credentials, but it sits more than DENSE_WORD_BEHIND, 0.05, behind signing, so it stays out.

cases.name: dense-band
why: signing and ceremony both name the subject, signing and key.
On words alone ceremony covers two of the three and clears HOOK_SCORE_FLOOR, 0.6 of the best lexical match.
With the encoder's cosine, ceremony at 0.82 sits more than DENSE_WORD_BEHIND, 0.05, behind signing at 1 and stays out.
